title: Of Offences Relating to Elections
shortDescription: Offences that corrupt free and fair elections: bribery (including treating), undue influence, personation, false statements about candidates, unauthorised campaign spending and failure to keep election accounts.

subHeadings.label: Punishment for bribery, undue influence and personation
False statements, illegal payments and accounts

summary:
Chapter IX protects the purity of elections. It corresponds to Chapter IXA of the IPC (ss.171A-171I), with the same nine provisions renumbered as ss.169-177 and some fines increased. The Gazette gives it no sub-headings; its sections fall into four groups: definitions (s.169), the three main offences defined (ss.170-172), their punishment (ss.173-174), and rules on campaign conduct and spending (ss.175-177).

Section 169 defines a 'candidate' (a person nominated at any election) and an 'electoral right' — the right to stand or not to stand, to withdraw, and to vote or not to vote. Because the right includes refraining, paying someone to stay away from the poll or forcing a candidate to withdraw is just as much an offence as buying a vote.

Three offences are defined first and punished afterwards. Bribery (s.170) is giving a gratification to induce or reward the exercise of an electoral right, or accepting one as such a reward; offers, agreements and attempts count, but a declaration of public policy or a promise of public action — the ordinary content of a manifesto — does not. Undue influence (s.171) is voluntarily interfering with the free exercise of an electoral right; threatening injury, or threatening divine displeasure or spiritual censure, is deemed interference. Personation (s.172) is voting or applying for a ballot paper in someone else's name, living or dead, or a fictitious name, or voting twice; an authorised proxy is excluded. Bribery is punishable with up to one year, or fine, or both, but 'treating' — bribery by food, drink, entertainment or provisions — is punishable with fine only (s.173). Undue influence and personation carry up to one year, or fine, or both (s.174).

The last three sections regulate campaign conduct. Publishing a false statement of fact about a candidate's personal character or conduct to affect the result is punishable with fine (s.175). Spending money to promote a candidate without his written authority is punishable with fine up to ₹10,000 (s.176), raised from ₹500 under the IPC. Failing to keep election accounts required by law is punishable with fine up to ₹5,000 (s.177). The punishments are light because corrupt practices also have serious consequences under the Representation of the People Act, 1951, such as setting aside an election and disqualification. Every offence in the Chapter is non-cognizable, bailable, not compoundable and triable by a Magistrate of the first class.

subPoints: 'Candidate' — nominated as a candidate at any election
'Electoral right' — to stand or not stand, withdraw, vote or refrain from voting
Giving a gratification to induce or reward the exercise of an electoral right
Accepting a gratification as such a reward, or for inducing others
Offering, agreeing or attempting counts as giving or accepting
Declaration of public policy or promise of public action is not bribery
Voluntary interference with the free exercise of an electoral right
Deemed: threat of injury of any kind; threat of divine displeasure or spiritual censure
Excluded: public policy, promise of public action, mere exercise of a legal right
Voting in another's name (living or dead) or a fictitious name
Voting twice at the same election
Abetting or procuring such voting
Authorised proxy excluded
Bribery: up to 1 year, or fine, or both
Treating (food, drink, entertainment, provision): fine only
Undue influence or personation: up to 1 year, or fine, or both
s.175 — false statement about a candidate's personal character or conduct: fine
s.176 — unauthorised election expenses: fine up to ₹10,000 (was ₹500)
s.176 proviso — up to ₹10 approved in writing within 10 days is deemed authorised
s.177 — failure to keep election accounts: fine up to ₹5,000 (was ₹500)
All offences: non-cognizable, bailable, triable by a Magistrate of the first class
None is compoundable

mindMap:
# Ch. IX — Offences Relating to Elections
## Definitions (s.169)
- Candidate
- Electoral right
  - Includes not voting
## Offences defined (ss.170-172)
- Bribery (s.170)
  - Giving / accepting gratification
  - Manifesto promises excluded
- Undue influence (s.171)
  - Threat of injury
  - Divine displeasure
- Personation (s.172)
  - Another's name / fictitious
  - Voting twice
  - Proxy excluded
## Punishment (ss.173-174)
- Bribery: 1 yr / fine
  - Treating: fine only
- Undue influence, personation: 1 yr / fine
## Campaign conduct (ss.175-177)
- False statement on candidate (s.175) — fine
- Unauthorised expenses (s.176) — ₹10,000
- No election accounts (s.177) — ₹5,000
## Classification
- Non-cognizable, bailable
- Magistrate first class
